title: Strict in_array() over a literal haystack narrows the needle to the string elements

ground_truth.statement: in_array($x, $y, true) compares with ===. In this fixture the haystack elements are 'a', 'b' or an int, so a true result means the needle is identical to one of them, and neither a bool nor a numeric string can be: for string|bool $x inside the guard, $x is 'a' or 'b'. Passing it to a parameter typed "a"|"b" is therefore sound, and no diagnostic belongs on that call.

notes: Mago 1.57.0 reports possibly-invalid-argument on the guarded call and describes the argument as numeric-string|'a'|'b', i.e. it reconciles the needle against a numeric-string alternative of the haystack even though the comparison is strict. PHPStan 2.3.1 and Psalm 6.20.0 narrow to 'a'|'b' and stay silent. The runtime script carries the asymmetric control the claim needs: the same needle/haystack pair under the default loose comparison matches ('1' is in [1]) while the strict form does not, so the third argument - not the values alone - is what makes the narrowing hold. The pattern was taken from mago/repro/strict-in-array-int-haystack-string-coercion/repro.php; the fixture is a clean-room rewrite.

sources.note: pattern source only; the claim was re-derived from the strict comparison semantics
